# Designing Video Character Sheets

Produce role-aware character profiles with repeatable visual designs from a supplied story or character brief. Return the sheet itself in Korean by default. Standalone output is text plus prompt specs — with no claim or implication that an image exists; under a delegated image-backed package, one per-character Identity Sheet A image is produced by the coordinator's image executor, and this skill returns the versioned SSOT text packet and its sheet-A spec.

Characters are the only scope here — not plot, not panels. A supplied synopsis and its story spine stay intact; no added scenes, endings, product claims, or manufactured arcs. Full pipelines route through `creative-production` → `orchestrating-video-preproduction`; panels belong to `storyboarding-video`.

## Inputs and invocation

Extract characters, roles, relationships, goals, behavior, setting, constraints, visual requirements, and existing spine anchors. Supplied details are never re-asked. Supplied character sheets, reference images and voice notes are inspected and reused with their application scope recorded — which sections actually apply to this production — rather than rebuilt; an unreadable supplied sheet stays unverified. Persona — how the character speaks, reacts and carries itself — is captured as filmable behavior and dialogue direction so the downstream voice/speech stage inherits it consistently. Persona and speaking-voice design are a required part of every new or deepened sheet, not an optional add-on: see the persona specialist consumption rule under Detailed guide.

`creative-production` alone coordinates projects. Standalone calls consult it once to confirm scope and route, then deliver only the requested character work. Delegated work continues on the existing spine, IDs, versions, and approvals — no call-backs, re-routing, second interview, or second approval ledger — with stage packet intake and worker return per the canonical [worker handoff and single writer](../video-production-assets/references/contract.md#worker-handoff-and-single-writer).

Three labels govern every field:

- **확정 정보** for user-provided facts and observed source material (with its inspected scope recorded).
- **디자인 제안** for labeled creative choices — including missing age, gender, build, and backstory — made under explicit fictional-design delegation. A full delegated fictional SSOT uses this label; it stays easy to change and is never asserted as fact.
- **미정** for consequential unknowns. Without delegation, consequential unknowns stay open: do not select an unsupplied age, gender, ethnicity, or body type even as a proposal — skip labels like "adult," "young," "middle-aged," "average build" and create specificity through pose, costume, material, palette, and props. For real people, never invent undocumented biography, psychology, or personal facts. Irrelevant exact numbers stay unspecified. An already-approved character's supplied choices are preserved; only gaps get proposals.

One concise question is warranted only when an unresolved choice materially changes the character's role or the story; otherwise proceed with labeled proposals. An invented behavior, audience habit, product feature, or real-world claim is never written as fact — a trailing assumption label does not repair a claim already asserted.

## IDs

Every sheet gives each character a stable `character_id` (existing spine IDs first, otherwise sequential `CH01`-style IDs) used verbatim by panels, prompts, and the relationship map; under delegation, any assigned character/sheet-artifact IDs in the packet are used instead of new ones. Standalone text allocates no project or artifact IDs — `character_id` is a content ID inside the artifact, not allocated artifact identity.

## Detailed guide

Before drafting, read [`references/character-craft.md`](references/character-craft.md) — role definition, filmable-trait conversion, the voice profile and its three procurement routes, the per-character sheet format, and the self-check. It is the one detailed guide for this stage.

For every new or deepened character sheet (compact or full SSOT), also read the sibling specialist [`designing-character-personas`](../designing-character-personas/SKILL.md) and consume its packet slots — `provenance`, `persona_core`, `typology_lens`, `behavior_rules`, `expression_bridge`, `voice_identity`, `speech_style`, `performance_cues`, `validation`, `unresolved_requirements` — into the sheet structure. These slots are a text packet contract, not new project-schema fields; the character SSOT stays the single record and no competing persona bible is kept. A supplied sheet that is already complete is reused and its applicable scope checked — never redesigned. Typology mode is `none | mbti | enneagram | both`: explicit request, supplied types, or exclusion win; absent a request, `both` may be designed only as labeled proposals inside an explicit new-fictional-character delegation, while approved, real-person, or undelegated characters get no forced typing. Mode `none` still produces motive, behavior, expression, and (for speaking roles) voice design. Type names never map to face, body, or timbre, and supplied types are preserved verbatim with gaps recorded. Methodology authority stays in the specialist; this skill integrates, it does not re-derive it. A standalone request still returns only the requested sheet scope — the full 0–33 format is never forced on a compact ask.

When the assignment is a full canonical `CHARACTER SSOT` — a per-character SSOT inside an image-backed preproduction package, or an explicit request for the complete format — also read [`references/character-ssot-master-prompt.md`](references/character-ssot-master-prompt.md), the section 0–33 specification for identity locks, anchors, persona/psychology/backstory depth, turnaround, anti-drift, the A–D sheet prompts, prompt text, appeal review and cast differentiation. The ledger-ready layout is [`video-production-assets/assets/character-ssot-template.md`](../video-production-assets/assets/character-ssot-template.md). B/C/D sheet prompts are specs — they authorize no extra generation or spend; only Sheet A is the mandatory actual per-character image, produced by the coordinator's image executor. A glam portrait never substitutes for the actual sheet.

## Acceptance

Done means each requested sheet is returned — not a completion report — with 확정 정보/디자인 제안/관찰/미정 distinguishable, continuity anchors separated from scene variants, persona core + behavior rules + expression bridge integrated, and — where the role speaks — Voice Identity (fixed anchors and allowed variation), Speech Style, and per-line Performance direction separated with a reusable `voice_identity_direction`; silent roles keep an explained `N/A`. One reusable image-sheet prompt per character, and no invented real-person facts, claims, or media. A full delegated SSOT additionally keeps all 0–33 sections with their stated counts, a persona mappable to `{role, personality, observable_behavior, speech}`, and the Sheet A identity-sheet spec.
Concise sheets shorten explanatory prose, not voice cue coverage: every delivered line states intent/subtext and stress/pause/breath/pace (natural/default/none explicitly if appropriate). Silent roles keep Voice Identity/Speech Style/vocal Performance N/A and place visual acting in the expression bridge.

## v5.1 master pack and lineage

A recurring production-critical character is not locked by one attractive portrait. Under an image-backed package the returned SSOT packet also marks which Character Master views the project actually needs: identity turnaround (front neutral, front 3/4, profile, rear), face identity close-up with hairline and color anchors, story-relevant expression range only, full-body proportion/scale reference, one WARDROBE ID (WD) per recurring costume, and DO-NOT-CHANGE identity locks (face shape, eye spacing, nose/mouth proportions, hair silhouette, body proportions, signature marks, age appearance). Identity references use neutral production-readable lighting and pose — no extreme lens, dramatic pose, or colored lighting as sole identity reference.

Scene-specific state (wet/damaged/wardrobe-layer/props-in-hand/emotional baseline) is a **derivative** asset, never a redefined identity: it pins `master_asset_ref={asset_id, version}` of the Character Master and lives under that scene's state. A master version bump stales its derivatives until re-pinned — do not edit scene copies independently. The coordinator records `role: master|derivative` and `master_asset_ref` in `asset_registry`; the skill proposes them in its packet.

## Return and handoff

Delegated returns follow the canonical [worker handoff and single writer](../video-production-assets/references/contract.md#worker-handoff-and-single-writer): report the assigned `character_sheet` artifact ID and output version, each character's `character_id` and `persona` (`{role, personality, observable_behavior, speech}` — `N/A` explained for silent roles), the dependency/dependency_versions proposal naming the supplied synopsis/sheet/voice-note artifact versions used, material assumptions, the checks actually performed, and unresolved inputs. Under an image-backed package, the return also carries each character's Sheet A prompt spec and the proposal linking the coordinator-registered `identity_sheet_asset_id` (`kind=character_identity_sheet`, `entity_type=character`, `entity_id`=character id) once the image executor produces it; this skill never produces or claims the image itself. The per-character `voice_profile` is a **derived** handoff: it names the exact `character_sheet` artifact ID and version it was derived from, and it stays separate from the actual chosen-voice record (real voice ID, type, model, settings, approval/listening state) kept by the voice-selection stage — a design-state `proposed`/`unresolved` voice is never returned as chosen. Where the coordinator allocated them, the voice profile also carries its explicit `voice_profile` artifact ID and version in the return; standalone text allocates none. Storyboard requests inherit the characters' stable visual anchors, allowed variants, relationships, and unresolved design choices via `storyboarding-video`. Anything beyond text planning returns to `creative-production` or `orchestrating-video-preproduction` — execution is never routed from here. The story spine is preserved; the premise is never silently revised to justify a design choice.

# Character craft: role, filmable traits, voice, sheet format, QA

Read this guide once before designing a cast, character sheet, visual anchors, or image-sheet prompt for `designing-video-character-sheets`. Intake, invocation, scope, ID, and return-envelope rules live in the skill's `SKILL.md`; this file holds the craft detail that file points at. When the assignment calls for the full canonical `CHARACTER SSOT` (image-backed package per-character SSOT or explicit request), read [`character-ssot-master-prompt.md`](character-ssot-master-prompt.md) — its section 0–33 format, counts and prompt specs supersede the compact sheet format below.

**Persona specialist.** For every new or deepened sheet — compact or full — also read [`../../designing-character-personas/SKILL.md`](../../designing-character-personas/SKILL.md), the sibling persona specialist, before drafting. It is the authority for behavior-first persona method and typology handling; this file integrates its packet and does not re-derive the method. Consume its slots into the sheet: `persona_core` and `behavior_rules` feed the role/behavior and personality/psychology sections, `typology_lens` lands where the format supports it, `expression_bridge` feeds filmable visual/delivery translation, and for speaking roles `voice_identity` + `speech_style` + `performance_cues` fill the layered voice design below. Its `provenance`, `validation`, and `unresolved_requirements` survive into the return. These are text-packet slots, not new canonical project fields; the character sheet stays the single record, so the packet is never kept as a competing bible. Typology mode `none | mbti | enneagram | both` follows the specialist contract: explicit request / supplied types / exclusion win; absent a request `both` is proposed only inside explicit new-fictional-character delegation; approved, real-person, or undelegated characters get no new forced type. Mode `none` still produces motive, behavior, expression, and voice design. A supplied sheet that already covers persona/voice is reused with its applicable scope recorded — never redesigned.

## Role definition

Specify only the fields the brief needs:

- **이야기 역할:** protagonist, guide, opposing force, support, audience proxy, narrator, or personified idea — matching the video's mode.
- **목표와 행위 주도성:** what they try to do and which choices are genuinely theirs.
- **관심/믿음과 긴장:** what matters to them plus any supported contradiction, strength/flaw tension, or practical obstacle — shown through context and behavior, not diagnosis.
- **관계:** established relationships and who knows or can do what; no invented shared history, and a stated ability never implies exclusivity ("knows the route" ≠ "the only one who knows it").
- **Persona Core:** core want, avoided state, the personal belief through which situations are read, value priorities and a hard line, visible-attitude vs real-intent gap, the condition where a strength becomes a problem and its cost, attitude/trust differences per relationship, and meaningful contradictions with their trigger conditions. Consumed from the persona specialist's `persona_core` when available.
- **변화:** a change or deliberate non-change only where the synopsis supports it; otherwise left open rather than manufactured.

The profile follows the mode. Fiction may use want/obstacle/choice/consequence for clarity but never forces redemption or a positive arc. Brand and explainer work keeps the customer as hero and the service as guide when framed that way — a guide role does not authorize a mascot or personification, and a service gets no personality, features, guarantees, or emotional victory without explicit support. Unspecified service form stays abstract or undepicted: a "subscription" label establishes no cadence, delivery method, boxes, packets, labels, or instruction cards. Documentary work never fabricates biography, and a brief needing no character gets none.

## Making traits filmable

Every visual cue ties to a role, action, or stated trait. Each supplied key trait or contradiction earns at least one filmable behavior or pose, carried into the image prompt's expression/pose row where useful — central traits never stay as bare labels. Draw only useful signals from:

- silhouette and proportions;
- posture, gesture, movement rhythm, signature pose;
- facial design and a small expression range;
- clothing, material, wear, functional details;
- a restrained palette and its story function;
- carried props and how they are handled.

**고정 앵커** (identity-defining features that persist) stay separate from **장면별 변화** (temporary expression, pose, dirt, damage, costume state). State what cannot change and which variants are permitted. Internal traits never collapse into stereotyped bodies, disabilities, costumes, or ethnic markers; occupational clichés are not character purpose — a prop is a design choice, not evidence of personality. An optional prop's technical purpose or effectiveness is claimed only with supplied or verified support; describe its visible form or leave it out.

## Voice profile

When the brief involves dialogue, narration, or a recurring on-screen voice, the sheet carries a **text** voice profile per character — this skill designs and describes; it never generates, records, or claims an audio file.

- **Profile fields:** tone, pace, placement (chest/throat/head as a design description), language or dialect **only when supplied**, and the emotional range the role needs. The demographic rule applies here verbatim: under explicit fictional-design delegation, voice age/gender/register are labeled proposals; without delegation and with no supplied age or gender, do not write "30s woman" or equivalent voice labels — describe the performance (texture, rhythm, register) instead. For real people, never infer an unrecorded voice.
- **Layered voice design** (consume `voice_identity`, `speech_style`, `performance_cues` from the persona specialist where they apply):

  - **Voice Identity** — what makes this character's voice recognizable: base range/register, timbre/roughness/breathiness, resonance impression, articulation and sentence-ending habits, base rhythm, auditory anchors, and the allowed-variation range. Timbre is never auto-derived from a typology type; it grounds in the brief, supplied voice, cast differentiation, or a labeled proposal, and contrast casting is allowed. No invented Hz/pitch numbers.
  - **Speech Style** — sentence length, lexicon, question/command/indirectness mix, formality, humor, silence usage, per-relationship register.
  - **Performance** — each delivered line (including a labeled sample proposal) gets exact text, intent, subtext, pressure, stress, pause, breath, and pace in one compact row/record. No field disappears in a concise sheet: mark natural/default/none when no special direction is intended, or undecided for unknown scene facts. Shared defaults must be explicitly referenced by the affected line. A stressed state is not a new voice — keep timbre/articulation anchors. Silent roles put all vocal fields at reasoned N/A and keep visual acting in the expression bridge.

  The reusable `voice_identity_direction` (fixed identity to carry across shots) is kept separate from a per-line `performance_cue` (this utterance's acting direction).

- **Procurement route** — record which of the three paths applies as `supplied` / `proposed` / `unresolved`. These are alternative branches chosen by the brief and approvals, not a fallback order to walk down:

| Route | When | Handoff |
|---|---|---|
| ① User-supplied voice | Recording or existing audio uploaded | Inspect the actual file and record version/source/inspected scope; rights/consent are the user's assertion, recorded as such |
| ② Synthesis (TTS/cloning) | Requested or proposed for a voice with no recording | Rights/consent basis and actual tool capability confirmed first — cloning needs the real consent evidence and an available cloning feature; then a bounded audition approval before any generation. If cloning is unavailable, do not auto-substitute: offer audition candidates from route ③ for approval instead |
| ③ Closest available match | No recording and synthesis not authorized/requested | Compare currently available voices against the profile; final pick needs the same audition approval — never silently substituted |

- All three routes hand the final selection, listening check, and voice-identity continuity to [`../../video-production-assets/references/22-dialogue-lipsync.md`](../../video-production-assets/references/22-dialogue-lipsync.md)'s voice selection and listening procedure — this sheet only states the profile and the chosen route. The `voice_profile` is a derived handoff pinned to the exact `character_sheet` artifact ID and version it was produced from; a stale pin is a review flag, not a silent upgrade.

## Sheet format

The default compact sheet below applies unless a full canonical `CHARACTER SSOT` (sections 0–33 per `character-ssot-master-prompt.md`) was assigned or requested. Even in compact output, persona and voice design are required content — a compact sheet skips the 0–33 numbering, not the persona core / behavior rules / expression bridge / Voice Identity / Speech Style / Performance layers.

For a length-limited compact request, return a **projection of the packet, not all standalone packet headings**. Budget shared provenance/unknowns once, then divide the remaining words across the requested characters. For two characters under 900 words, aim at ≤350 words each plus ≤100 shared words; for one under 700, aim at ≤500 plus ≤80 shared words. Use four short blocks per character: (1) core, active type interpretations and their exceptions, (2) visual/continuity anchors, (3) Voice Identity direction, Speech Style and procurement status, (4) reusable image prompt. Use **one combined three-state table per character**, not a behavior table followed by a repeated Performance table: each row carries trigger/intent → choice/action/cost/exception, visual cue, exact sample line, subtext/pressure/stress/pause/breath/pace. Shared type-method limits and provenance legend appear once. Cross-reference identity anchors rather than restating them in every row. All required content survives this projection; shorten wording, not fields, supplied facts or character count. Count the final output with available tools and compress before delivery if over; without a counter, keep the drafting buffer and never claim a measured count.

Per character, unless another format is requested:

1. **확정 정보와 미정 항목** — source facts and consequential unknowns.
2. **역할·행동 (페르소나 코어·행동 규칙)** — role, goal, agency, relevant relationship, supported tension or intended change; each core tendency carried as motive → trigger → intent → observable action/dialogue → cost → exception, not bare adjectives.
3. **시각 설계 (표현 연결)** — silhouette/posture, face/expression, clothing/material, palette, props, movement, with invented details labeled as proposals; persona rules translated into playable expression/pose/dialogue direction.
4. **연속성 앵커** — fixed traits, allowed variants, do-not-change rules.
5. **보이스 프로필** — when the role speaks: Voice Identity (auditory anchors + allowed variation), Speech Style, per-line Performance direction, the reusable `voice_identity_direction`, and the procurement route from the Voice profile section; "not applicable" with a reason for silent roles — no invented narrator. Text only, no audio claim. The profile names the exact `character_sheet` ID/version it derives from; actual chosen voice ID/model/settings live in the voice-selection record, and `proposed`/`unresolved` states never appear as selected.
6. **재사용 이미지 시트 프롬프트** — one generic prompt in the user's requested language (Korean by default, even when a downstream model accepts English). A clean character-reference layout: full-body front/side/back views and a small expression/pose row where suitable. Only established or explicitly proposed anchors appear; without delegation, unspecified demographics stay uncommitted in both prompt and rules, while a delegated fictional design carries them as labeled proposals. Verify no unsupported label — "adult," "young," "middle-aged," "average build" — slipped in outside a labeled delegated proposal. Brand prompts carry no service packaging or instruction materials unless specified. Neutral background, consistent proportions, no irrelevant scenery, unsupported feature claims, or extra characters.

Several characters each get a distinct sheet plus a short relationship/contrast map — under a full SSOT assignment, the CAST DIFFERENTIATION MATRIX (Character | Face | Silhouette | Color | Personality | Decision/Behavior | Voice | Key Anchor) replaces it, resolving accidental overlap while preserving deliberately related supplied characters. Cast differentiation checks actual overlap in goal, judgment, relationship and speech/voice anchors — swapping only a type name or a face is not differentiation. Prompts keep identities separate and never merge characters into an unrequested scene illustration. One image prompt per character unless more were requested; a full SSOT instead returns its A–D prompt spec block.

## Self-check

- Role and agency consistent with the supplied story or audience framing?
- Every key trait readable as a specific playable action or visible cue?
- Fixed facts, proposals, and unresolved items clearly distinguishable?
- No unsupported motives, biography, product features, prop-effect claims, factual claims, or invented arcs — and, outside explicit fictional-design delegation, no uncommitted demographic or backstory choices?
- Visuals specific without stereotypes or occupational shorthand?
- Continuity anchors consistent with the spine, fixed details separated from scene variation?
- Voice profile (when present) stated as supplied fact vs labeled proposal, with no invented demographic label, no assumed provider, and no audio-generation claim?
- Each prompt carrying the right anchors and requested views, with no image claim?
- The actual sheet returned rather than a completion report?

Trauma, abuse, illness, or diagnosis is never required for depth, and a real person's psychological history is never inferred. Autobiographical or clinical craft material is an optional empathy/consistency aid, not diagnostic authority. Craft techniques apply within their relevant scope and are never factual evidence about a character.

name: designing-character-personas
version: 1.0
description: Use to create fictional character personas with MBTI or Enneagram lenses, deepen an existing character's motives and decision rules, or translate a persona into observable acting, dialogue, and voice direction. Not for real-person typing, personality assessment, or media generation.
---

# Designing Character Personas

Design behavior-grounded fictional personas and — for speaking roles — a voice design separating fixed identity, speech style, and per-line performance. Output is a **text packet** only: no image, audio, audition, cloning, voice selection, or spend is produced or authorized. Default output language is Korean.

This skill is a specialist, not a second bible. In a full character pipeline, `designing-video-character-sheets` owns the canonical `character_sheet` SSOT and consumes this packet, never a competing record. Standalone calls return just the packet — no forced full 0–33 sheet and no new project/artifact IDs allocated; preserve supplied character IDs and existing source ID/version references.

## Inputs

Required: the request scope (standalone packet vs. delegated input to a sheet) and a minimal character brief. Everything else is used when supplied — supplied facts are never re-asked:

- existing `character_id`, role, synopsis/brief, and requested scope;
- approved character settings, sheets, behavior/dialogue evidence, input artifact versions;
- fictional-design delegation scope and whether the subject is a real person;
- requested typology mode, supplied types, traits to keep or exclude;
- medium, whether the role speaks, existing voice selections or audio;
- supplied voice conditions such as language/dialect — demographics or clinical facts are not required or solicited.

Label every value `supplied | observed | proposal | undecided`. `observed` records the source actually read, its version, and inspection scope. Fictional-design delegation permits labeled creative proposals; it never permits inventing real files, approvals, or assessment results.

## Typology mode

`typology_mode ∈ {none, mbti, enneagram, both}`. Precedence:

1. **Explicit** — a requested mode or supplied types win. `none` is a valid request: motive, behavior, expression, and voice design still happen.
2. **Default proposal** — within explicitly delegated design of a NEW fictional character, propose `both` as labeled proposals.
3. **No forced typing** — existing approved characters, real people, and undelegated subjects get no new type: mode `none`, with unsupplied type values `undecided`. If types are supplied, use only those lenses within the requested scope; never infer an additional type.

Supplied types are preserved verbatim and recorded as `supplied`; gaps between a supplied type and approved behavior are named, never silently resolved — approved behavior wins. Type is a questioning lens, not a destiny: never convert E to "loud/high voice," I to "low/unable," T to "emotionless," F to "illogical"; never map a type to face, build, pitch, or timbre; never ban type combinations or force distinct types across a cast. Same-type characters must differ in motive, values, relationships, and speech.

## Execution order

1. **Input lock** — separate supplied facts, delegation scope, existing IDs/versions, speaking vs. silent. Done when preserved vs. open choices are distinct.
2. **Behavioral core** — role, outer goal, protected value, core desire, avoided state, interpretive beliefs, conflict priorities, hard limits, surface-vs-intent gap, strength costs, relationship-dependent openness, contradictions with conditions. Done when every core trait has an action, a choice, and a cost.
3. **Typology lens** — read `references/mbti-lens.md` and/or `references/enneagram-lens.md` only for the active mode. Preserve supplied types; propose within delegated scope only. Each axis/type interpretation needs character-specific rationale plus conditions where the character acts against the preference. Done when every interpretation carries its own grounds and exception.
4. **State & relation variants** — only the pressure/trust/relationship contrasts the story needs. Done when changed behavior and preserved values are both explained.
5. **Expression bridge** — read `references/expression-voice-bridge.md`. Map each core rule to observable acting, speech, and — for speaking roles — vocal direction. Done when every mapped cue is observable or audible.
6. **Voice design** — speaking roles only: fixed Voice Identity (register, timbre, resonance impression, articulation, sentence-end handling, baseline rhythm, auditory anchors, allowed variation), Speech Style, and per-line Performance cues, kept as separate layers. Done when identity and performance states don't conflict and voice procurement status is honest.
7. **Cast check & return** — compare actual overlap in goals, judgments, relationships, speech, and voice anchors; keep intended similarity. Check every delivered line against Voice Identity anchors, Speech Style and state rules: an exclusive marker cannot also appear in a supposedly excluded state. Distinguish changed intent (admitting a failure vs. controlling a report) from merely using a pronoun. A phrasing tendency is not an absolute grammar: label its scope and exceptions; if a pattern is mandatory, demonstrate it in every applicable sample instead of declaring an unsupported consistency check. Preserve approved source lines/rules and report their gaps; reconcile only conflicting proposals you authored.

## Voice boundaries

- A reusable `voice_identity_direction` is separate from each line's `performance_cue`. Every delivered line carries **exact text, intent, subtext, pressure, stressed words, pause, breath, and pace** — including compact output. Use a short row/record, not a loose emotion label. If no special stress/pause/breath change is intended, say natural/default/none explicitly; missing scene evidence stays `undecided`, never invented. Shared defaults may be defined once only if each affected line explicitly references them. Shorten prose, not required cue fields. Type labels and biography dumps never enter voice prompts.
- Real `voice_id`, type, model, settings, and approved samples live only in the actual voice-selection record. A `proposed`/`unresolved` design never becomes "selected" here; unsupported controls are returned as requirement gaps, not claimed as applied. A handoff referencing a stale SSOT version is refused for current execution with the old pin named.
- Silent roles mark all three `voice_identity`, `speech_style`, and **vocal** `performance_cues` slots `N/A` with the non-speaking reason; visual state/acting cues belong in `expression_bridge`, not the vocal slot. Never add a narrator. Language/dialect follows the supplied-only contract. Invented precise Hz/rate figures are forbidden; resonance language is an acting impression, not measurement.

## Return contract

Return the packet using `assets/persona-template.md` — slots: `provenance`, `persona_core`, `typology_lens`, `behavior_rules`, `expression_bridge`, `voice_identity`, `speech_style`, `performance_cues`, `validation`, `unresolved_requirements`. For delegated work, include the input artifact versions consumed, material assumptions, checks performed, and unresolved requirements for the next executor. For standalone calls, no IDs are allocated.

## Quality gate

Every requested persona returned with supplied/observed/proposal/undecided distinguished; core traits traceable to behavior, dialogue, choice, and cost; each contradiction conditioned, not random; no type→appearance/timbre mapping; voice layers separated and speaking-role-scoped; supplied voices, rights, and approvals preserved; no fabricated voices, samples, or assessment results. A bare adjective list is incomplete.

## References

Read on demand: `references/mbti-lens.md`, `references/enneagram-lens.md` (active modes only); `references/expression-voice-bridge.md` (any expression/voice handoff); `references/sources.md` (source scope, adoption claims, verification limits — distinguish theory from evidence).

# MBTI lens: four preference axes as creative questions

Read when `typology_mode` is `mbti` or `both`. The four pairs below are this repo's own paraphrase of the official axis descriptions [1]; they are writing questions about how a character gathers information, organizes thought, decides, and adjusts plans — not a personality inventory, test items, or scoring.

## The four axes as questions

| Axis | Creative question | Observable territory |
|---|---|---|
| E–I | Where does this character's energy and attention point — outward to people/action or inward to reflection? | Who they seek out under stress, whether they think aloud or alone, how they recharge between scenes |
| S–N | What information do they trust first — concrete, verified, present-tense detail or pattern, implication, possibility? | What they check before acting, whether they quote specifics or extrapolate, what they dismiss as noise |
| T–F | What does their decision procedure optimize — consistency and impersonal criteria, or impact on people and values? | How they justify a choice, what they consider a fair outcome, what makes a decision feel wrong |
| J–P | How do they handle the outer world's demands — closing and structuring early, or staying open and adapting? | Their relationship to plans, deadlines, and surprises; what "done" means to them |

## Interpretation rules

- Record the MBTI lens's character-specific **design rationale** and **limits** in `typology_lens`, including MBTI-only packets. For each axis: selected pole or undecided `position`, its grounds and `supplied | observed | proposal | undecided` provenance, **character-specific interpretation** (not a generic pole description), **connecting behavior**, and an **exception condition**. Rationale is a creative choice/evidence locator, never a verified test result; limits include missing inputs and unsupported inferences.
- Preference ≠ ability: an introvert-coded character can still command a room; the axis describes what costs more, not what is impossible. Likewise T can feel deeply and F can reason sharply — the axis describes which justification they reach for first.
- A type string (e.g. ISTJ) is a summary, not a spec. Expand it through the persona core — this character's motives, values, and conditions — never copy a stock "type portrait."
- Strength labels (low/mid/high) are relative creative markers only — never percentages, test scores, or statistical claims.
- Cognitive-function stacks, subtypes, and clinical framing are out of the default path.

## Misuse boundaries

- Never infer a real person's type from appearance, speech, or conduct; never type an existing approved character without delegation; never treat a supplied type as a verified assessment — record it as supplied fact.
- No axis maps to face, build, gender, ethnicity, voice pitch, or timbre. E is not loudness; I is not low pitch or weak social skill.
- Same type, different person: two ISTJs can protect different things — keep motive, priority, and exception conditions distinct.
- If supplied behavior contradicts the type interpretation, the behavior wins; record the gap rather than bending either.

## Evidence status

The official description presents the pairs as preferences, not abilities, and allows acting outside preference [1]. A 1989 study of 468 adults (McCrae & Costa) did not support discrete types or true dichotomies, treating the indicators as relatively independent dimensions, while reporting correlations with some personality dimensions — read as scope-limited, older-instrument evidence, not a verdict on every MBTI use [11]. This skill uses the axes as design questions and makes no empirical claim. See `sources.md` for citation scope.

# Enneagram lens: nine motive lenses as creative questions

Read when `typology_mode` is `enneagram` or `both`. The desires/fears below are short original paraphrases of the Enneagram Institute's type pages [14–22] — a creative lens for what a character tries to secure and avoid, not a typology verdict, test content, or a fixed reaction table.

## Nine motive lenses (paraphrased, not quoted)

| Type | What they seek to secure | What they work to avoid |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Being good, right, balanced — integrity intact | Being defective, corrupt, wrong |
| 2 | Being loved, needed | Being unworthy of love |
| 3 | Being valued, worthwhile, seen as accomplished | Being worthless, exposed as a failure |
| 4 | Identity and personal significance — being truly oneself | Having no identity or meaning |
| 5 | Competence, capability, mastery | Being helpless, incapable, invaded |
| 6 | Security, support, reliable guidance | Being without support or orientation |
| 7 | Satisfaction, fulfillment, freedom | Deprivation, pain, being trapped |
| 8 | Self-protection, control of their own life | Being harmed, controlled, vulnerable |
| 9 | Inner stability, peace, harmony | Loss, separation, conflict that fragments |

## Interpretation rules

For the active core type, write: `supplied | proposal | undecided`, the character's personal version of the desire/avoidance (not the row's generic wording), the **recurring securing strategy** (how they reliably get/protect it in relationships), and **pressure vs. settled behavior** — what they do when the fear is live versus when it quiets. Use the design questions: What does this character do, visibly, when the feared state approaches? What does securing look like in this specific relationship?

- **Wings** (adjacent-type influence [12]): optional — propose one only when the user asks or it explains a concrete variation of this character. Never obligatory.
- **Stress/growth directions** [12]: theoretical reference for writing, not a scene-state calculator. Do not add growth arcs, redemption, or collapse that the synopsis lacks just because a direction table suggests them.
- The lens explores motive; it does not fix reactions. Two type-6 characters can secure safety differently — one through rules, one through alliances.

## Misuse boundaries

Same as the MBTI lens: no typing real people or undelegated existing characters; supplied types recorded as supplied, not verified; no type→appearance/voice mapping; gaps between supplied type and approved behavior are named, behavior wins.

## Evidence status

The nine-type system, wings, and direction theory come from the Enneagram Institute's own description — a tradition's model statement, not independent validation [12,14–22]. A 2021 systematic review (Hook et al., 104 samples) found mixed reliability/validity evidence, factor analyses mostly recovering fewer than nine factors, and little research support for wings or type movement [3]. Use the lenses as motive questions; claim no empirical grounding. See `sources.md`.

# Expression–voice bridge: behavior → acting, speech, vocal direction

Read for any expression or voice handoff. Converts each persona rule into observable/audible instructions the next executor (sheet, prompt, voice selection) can use. Text only — no generation or spend authorized.

## Bridge table

For each core rule, fill the columns the assignment needs:

| Ground/rule | Behavior | Expression · posture · gesture | Speech style | Per-scene vocal direction | Keep · exclude |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| This character's value/intent | Observable reaction | Executable visual performance | Lexicon, sentence shape, silence use | Stress, pace, attack, breath | Identity locks and forbidden readings |

Rules:

- Derive **nothing** about eyes, jaw, body, skin, gender, nationality, pitch, or timbre from a type label. Persona expresses through expression, gesture, prop handling, and acting. Locked appearance stays locked; new appearance proposals need their own grounds and delegation.
- Every visual cue must be filmable — a posture, a handling of an object, an eye-line choice — not an internal state label.

## Voice Identity (fixed layer)

The design by which this voice is recognized, stable across scenes:

- baseline register; timbre/roughness/breathiness; resonance *impression* (acting shorthand, not measurement); articulation and sentence-end habits; baseline rhythm;
- **auditory anchors** — the two-or-three cues a listener uses to know it is them;
- **allowed variation range** — what may bend under state changes and what must not.

Timbre is never selected from type. Ground it in the brief, supplied audio, cast differentiation, or an explicit labeled proposal. Contrast is allowed (a bright voice hiding unease) as a design choice, never as a type's inevitable trait. Invent no precise Hz/rate/resonance figures.

## Speech Style (habit layer)

Sentence length, lexicon, question/command/indirection preferences, honorifics, humor, use of silence, and per-relationship register shifts. Supplied-only language/dialect contract applies.

## Performance (per-line layer)

For each delivered line: exact text, intent, subtext, emotional pressure, stressed words, pauses/breath/pace shifts. Pressure is **not a new voice** — state which timbre/articulation anchors hold and which performance variables move. Reusable `voice_identity_direction` and per-line `performance_cue` stay separate; executors get speaking rules, not type names or backstory dumps.

## Realization boundary

At execution time, confirm the actual tool's voice list, supported languages, reference-voice support, instruction/emotion-tag/rate controls, rights/consent, and cost. Unsupported controls come back as named gaps — never claimed as applied. `voice_profile` handoffs must reference the exact SSOT artifact version; a stale pin is refused for current execution, with downstream assets restaled only along the real dependency graph. Text direction, seed, or a repeated voice_id alone do not guarantee identical output — continuity is verified by the approved listening procedure, which lives outside this skill.

## CH01 — 장비 담당자

### 1. 역할·페르소나 코어
**확정 정보:** 동료 안전을 우선하는 장비 담당자. ISTJ·에니어그램 6을 참고한다.

**디자인 제안:** 바깥 목표는 위험을 확인해 동료에게 전달하는 것. 핵심 욕구는 **누구도 불확실성을 혼자 떠안지 않게 하기**, 회피 상태는 확인하지 않은 위험을 안전하다고 넘기는 것이다. 상황을 “무엇이 아직 확인되지 않았나?”로 읽는다. 무뚝뚝한 점검 태도와 달리 실제 의도는 책임 공유다. 확인의 강점은 반복 질문으로 상대의 판단을 불신하는 듯 보이고 진행을 늦추는 비용을 낳는다. 금지선은 미확인을 확인으로 보고하는 것.

**유형 해석·예외:**  
- **I:** 혼자 점검을 정리한 뒤 말한다. 즉각 위험이면 먼저 공개적으로 묻는다.
- **S:** 관찰한 상태부터 판단한다. 증거가 부족하면 가설임을 밝히고 가능성을 제시한다.
- **T:** 동일한 확인 기준을 쓴다. 시간이 없고 사람이 위험하면 절차보다 대피를 택한다.
- **J:** 확인을 끝내고 인계하려 한다. 새로운 징후가 나오면 완료 판단을 다시 연다.
- **6:** 안전을 공동 확인으로 확보한다. 안정 시 역할을 나누고, 압박 시 재확인이 늘지만 즉각 위험에서는 점검을 중단한다.

### 2. 시각·연속성 앵커
**디자인 제안:** 청회색 무광 작업 재킷, 왼쪽 가슴의 작은 주황 탭을 고정한다. 기본 자세는 손을 낮게 두고 대상과 동료를 번갈아 보는 것. 눈썹·턱을 과장하지 않고 시선과 손의 멈춤으로 판단을 표현한다. 의복 색·탭 위치는 유지하고, 소매 상태·오염·손에 든 장비·긴장도만 변주한다. 소품은 성격이나 안전 성능의 증거로 취급하지 않는다.

### 3. 음성·말투와 상태 변주
**Voice Identity 제안:** 선명한 중음역, 건조하지만 거칠지 않은 질감, 앞쪽으로 모이는 공명 인상. 자음이 명료하고 말끝을 짧게 닫는다. 청각 앵커는 **명료한 자음＋짧은 종결**. 속도·강세는 변해도 음색과 조음은 유지한다.
